author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Dover will dedicate a new permanent 9/11 memorial Friday as the city marks 25 years since the September 11, 2001, terrorist attacks.

The remembrance ceremony is scheduled for 11 a.m. September 11 in the Cocheco Mill Courtyard on Central Avenue, according to a city announcement posted Tuesday. The dedication gives Dover a fixed public site for future remembrance in addition to this year’s anniversary program.

The timing places the local ceremony within a week of memorial events across New Hampshire and the country. Dover’s announcement centers its observance on both remembrance and the formal unveiling of the memorial rather than a temporary display.

Residents planning to attend should check the city’s event notice for any logistical updates before traveling downtown. The city had not described a weather alternative or changes to the 11 a.m. start in the posted notice. The event comes on a milestone anniversary when communities are also considering how to preserve firsthand memory for younger residents who were born after the attacks.
dek: The city plans an 11 a.m. remembrance ceremony Friday in the Cocheco Mill Courtyard, where its new memorial will be dedicated.
headline: Dover to dedicate permanent 9/11 memorial on 25th anniversary
